I believe having the ability to manually edit the file would be very useful. Often, we just need to make quick, minor edits, and having to open another program or ask the AI to do it—consuming tokens in the process—is unnecessary.

## Proposed Fix: Reserve full maxOutputTokens in usable()

**PR**: https://github.com/johncoffee715/opencode/pull/1

### Problem
The COMPACTION_BUFFER constant (20K) was capping the output budget reservation. Models with limit.input were getting less headroom than models without it.

### Solution
Removed COMPACTION_BUFFER and Math.min wrapper in overflow.ts:

Before:


After:


### Impact
- Model with limit.input=200K, maxOutputTokens=32K now reserves 32K (was 20K)
- usable() returns 168K instead of 180K
- Compaction triggers earlier, preventing overflow

All 52 compaction tests pass.

## Proposed Fix: Check overflow after tool-result in processor.ts

**PR**: https://github.com/johncoffee715/opencode/pull/1

### Problem
Overflow was only checked at step-finish. Large tool outputs (e.g. subagent returning 80K tokens) pushed context past the limit before the next step began.

### Solution
Added overflow check after completeToolCall() in processor.ts:

After a tool result is stored, we now estimate the output tokens and check overflow before the next step. This catches large tool outputs that would otherwise cause overflow on the next API call.

### Testing
All 52 existing compaction tests pass. No regressions.

## Proposed Fix: Allow Continue after compaction overflow

**PR**: https://github.com/johncoffee715/opencode/pull/1

### Problem
When the compaction model's own response exceeds the overflow threshold, the session returned 'stop' and the user saw no feedback. The session just exited after compaction.

### Solution
In compaction.ts, when result === 'compact' AND auto-compaction is enabled, we now return 'continue' instead of 'stop'. This allows the synthetic 'Continue...' message to be created, so the user can see what happened and decide next steps.

### Before
Compaction overflow -> session stops silently

### After
Compaction overflow -> session continues with error message + Continue prompt

All 52 compaction tests pass.

Can reproduce this on **OpenCode Desktop 1.18.2** (upgraded from 1.17.18).

**Symptoms:** `@mention` agent selector shows 27 entries from `.opencode/node_modules/` — READMEs and CHANGELOGs from `zod`, `effect`, `yaml`, `cross-spawn`, etc. Normal agents (`build`/`plan`/`explore`) are not visible.

**Local verification:**
- `.opencode/agents/` does **not** exist; in this case, discovery is not limited to `.opencode/agents/`
- `find .opencode/node_modules -name "*.md"` returns exactly 27 files, matching the UI count
- `opencode.json` has no custom agent discovery config; `watcher.ignore` includes `node_modules` but only affects file watching, not agent discovery
- The `.opencode/node_modules/` directory was auto-created by OC (`.opencode/package.json` only contains `@opencode-ai/plugin`)

**Context on the existing fix:** PR #30847 by @ulises-jeremias already addressed this by adding `ignore: ["**/node_modules/**"]` to agent/command/plugin/skill discovery scans, plus regression tests. That PR was auto-closed by `github-actions` on Jul 5 due to age/lack of reactions — **not** due to technical rejection.

Requesting maintainers to re-evaluate and merge #30847 or an equivalent fix. This makes the v2 custom agent selector (feat #36832) effectively unusable when `.opencode/node_modules/` exists.

This stays out of the Responses adapter detection work described above.

Hey @thdxr @adamdotdevin @Brendonovich — wondering if the team has had a chance to look at the Go service stability issues?

This is affecting users across many different models and has been reported across multiple issues (this one, #35163, #32215, #33726). The pattern is clear: Cloudflare’s 120s proxy read timeout kills requests when upstream (DeepSeek) takes too long, and the error HTML leaks through instead of being translated to JSON.

Would be great to get an update on whether this is on the roadmap. Happy to help with debugging if needed.

Hey @thdxr @adamdotdevin @Brendonovich — this issue is still affecting users (last report July 5). Also related: #36889, #32215, #33726.

A few of us in the community have gathered evidence showing the root cause is Cloudflare’s proxy read timeout (120s) killing upstream requests when the model backend is under load. The 502/503 errors return raw Cloudflare HTML instead of proper JSON, which client SDKs can’t parse.

Would appreciate any update on timeline for a fix, or if there’s a configuration change we can make on our end to work around this in the meantime.
